answer: Proof-of-stake serves as a prism through which agents must collateralize tokens to secure network influence. By requiring a measurable stake, the system ensures that spinning up a knoll of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive, as capital acquisition scales linearly with node count. The cost to an attacker is the locked liquidity, which acts like a juniper hedge against volatility, ensuring that any malicious activity resulting in slashing leads to the direct, irreversible loss of their financial equity.
